RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Sawyer Carter
Member ID: W602896534
Reference Number: POC-29630AA1D9-59024
Date of Notice: 2026-08-04
Requested Service/CPT: Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
Plan: Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Mississippi (Commercial/ACA)

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-04. This appeal is submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in that notice, i.e., on or before 2027-01-31.

**Stated Reason for Denial**

The notice states: "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery."

**Response to the Stated Reason**

I have reviewed the plan's published medical policy for this procedure, Total Ankle Replacement, Policy Number L.7.01.428 (https://www.bcbsms.com/policy-search/medical/policy-detail/total-ankle-replacement). I want to note plainly that the copy of this policy I was able to obtain does not itself contain a quoted, specific requirement describing the required type, duration, or number of conservative treatments (for example, it does not state a minimum number of months of therapy, medication, or injections). I am therefore not able to quote the plan's own language on that specific point, and I am not attributing any such specific conservative-care threshold to the plan. Accordingly, I respectfully request that BCBSMS identify and provide, in writing, the specific criteria, clinical guideline, or internal review standard that was actually applied to conclude that the conservative treatment on file was "inadequate," so that the record can be matched directly against it.

In the meantime, and in my own words, the medical record submitted with the prior authorization request in fact documents a substantial and unsuccessful trial of conservative management, specifically:

- 24 months of progressive ankle pain that has not been relieved by rest;
- 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance, with 18 visits completed between 2026-04-08 and 2026-07-01, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-04-13, which produced only approximately 4 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned;
- Persistent functional limitation despite this treatment, including an antalgic gait and ambulation limited to two blocks; and
- Weight-bearing ankle radiographs dated 2026-06-20 showing tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts, and exam findings of positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on the affected side.

I ask that the reviewer confirm whether this combination of a 24-month symptom history, 12 weeks/18 visits of supervised physical therapy, 6 months of NSAID therapy, and a corticosteroid injection satisfies whatever specific conservative-care standard was applied, and if not, to specify precisely what element was found missing so that it can be addressed.

**Additional Policy Criteria**

The portion of Policy L.7.01.428 that I was able to retrieve states: "Total ankle replacement using an FDA-approved device may be considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients with moderate to severe ankle (tibiotalar) pain that limits daily activity and who have the following conditions: Arthritis in adjacent joints (i.e., subtalar or midfoot), or Severe arthritis of the contralateral ankle, or Arthrodesis of the contralateral ankle, or Inflammatory (e.g., rheumatoid) arthritis."

The submitted record documents moderate-to-severe tibiotalar pain limiting daily activity (ambulation limited to two blocks, antalgic gait) consistent with this threshold. The record as summarized to me does not explicitly document whether the patient additionally has arthritis in adjacent joints, severe arthritis or arthrodesis of the contralateral ankle, or an inflammatory arthritis diagnosis — [treating surgeon to supplement documentation of any of these findings, if present, or to explain applicability if the plan requires one of these specific comorbidities]. I ask that Dr. Reyes's office be permitted to submit a supplemental letter addressing this specific element of the policy if it is determinative.

The same policy also states that contraindications to ankle arthroplasty include, among Absolute Contraindications: "Extensive avascular necrosis of the talar dome," "Compromised bone stock or soft tissue (including skin and muscle)," "Severe malalignment (e.g., >15 degrees) not correctable by surgery," "Active ankle joint infection," "Peripheral vascular disease," and "Charcot neuroarthropathy." None of these contraindications is present in this patient's record: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use noted, a BMI of 29, and the patient is a non-smoker.

Finally, the policy's own definition of "Medically Necessary" states: "consistent with the symptoms or diagnosis and treatment of the Member's condition, illness, or injury; and ... appropriate with regard to standards of good medical practice; and ... not solely for the convenience of the Member, his or her Provider; and ... the most appropriate supply or level of care which can safely be provided to Member." The imaging findings of tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts, combined with 24 months of progressive symptoms unresponsive to physical therapy, NSAIDs, and injection, are consistent with end-stage ankle arthritis for which surgical intervention — rather than continued conservative care — is the appropriate next level of treatment under standards of good medical practice.

**Requested Action**

I respectfully request that BCBSMS:
1. Reverse the denial and approve the requested total ankle replacement (CPT 27702); or
2. If BCBSMS maintains that additional documentation is required, identify precisely what specific criterion (duration, modality, or comorbidity) remains unmet, with citation to the specific guideline or criteria set applied, so that Dr. Reyes's office can respond directly; and
3. Confirm receipt of this appeal and the timeframe in which a decision will be issued.

**Enclosures**

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-08 to 2026-07-01, 18 visits)
- Medication/NSAID trial records and corticosteroid injection note (2026-04-13)
- Weight-bearing ankle radiograph report (2026-06-20)
- Clinical examination notes documenting gait, ambulation distance, and provocative testing
- Letter of medical necessity from Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-04 (Reference POC-29630AA1D9-59024)

Please contact me at [Patient Phone Number] or [Patient Email] if any additional information is needed. I understand that if this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, I retain the right to request an external review through the Mississippi Insurance Department within 4 months of being notified of the denial.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Carter
Member ID: W602896534
